text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH - inference-pool-usw-2 reporting multiple NotReady nodes and elevated 5xxs. Impact: some inference requests failing with 502/503, p50/p95 latency spike. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/infer/overview
Shilpa: I'm on it — joining. any affected customers called out? :pager:
Matt R: Saw alert on dashboards: 5xx rate ~12% for the pool, p50 ~1.2s, p95 ~3.8s, error budget creeping. Might be serving runtime/container crashes.
Priya: kubelet restarts on a couple nodes in last 6m. Checking node states now.
Priya: output from `kubectl get nodes -o wide`:
```
node_gpu_01   Ready     v1.27.3   10.10.1.12   inference-pool-usw-2   <none>   24d
node_gpu_03   NotReady  v1.27.3   10.10.1.14   inference-pool-usw-2   KubeletNotReady   00:06:23
node_gpu_07   NotReady  v1.27.3   10.10.1.18   inference-pool-usw-2   KubeletNotReady   00:05:47
node_gpu_09   NotReady  v1.27.3   10.10.1.20   inference-pool-usw-2   KubeletNotReady   00:04:12
```
Dawn: SSHing node_gpu_03 now, grabbing kubelet and kernel logs.
Dawn: dmesg snippet shows GPU/driver and oom signs:
```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.457000] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 28941 (run_infer) score 123
[  123.457120] kubelet: E0215 10:12:18.789  1234 remote_runtime.go:xxx] runtime service crashed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start container: container_linux.go:xxx: [..] device plugin init error
```
Matt R: Xid 79 usually indicates GPU driver crash. Could be driver/kernel mismatch or memory pressure from a runaway job. What's running on those nodes? Any huge batch jobs?
Priya: Looking at pod list on node_gpu_03: several heavy inference pods pinned to GPUs, plus one unknown training job that snuck into pool last night (label mismatch).
Shilpa: Immediate plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) drain pods to new nodes (force if needed), 3) scale up pool by +2 replicas, 4) restart kubelet on recovered nodes, 5) shift traffic away from pool via routing policy to reduce impact. Who wants steps?
Matt R: I'll handle routing and quick scale. Priya/Dawn: do cordon/drain and attempt kubelet restart. Shilpa: I'll coordinate customer comms and handoff.
Priya: cordoning node_gpu_03 and node_gpu_07 now:
```
$ kubectl cordon node_gpu_03
node/node_gpu_03 cordoned
$ kubectl cordon node_gpu_07
node/node_gpu_07 cordoned
```
Priya: drain on node_gpu_03 failing due to pods with local shared-device-plugin and eviction blocked. Using force delete to unblock, will recreate on new nodes.
Priya: commands run:
```
$ kubectl drain node_gpu_03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
Warning: deleting pods
pod/infer-xyz-1 deleted
pod/infer-abc-5 deleted
```
Infra Bot: autoscaler: scaling group inference-usw-2 +2 instances requested, starting provisioning (aws://eu-west-1/instancegroup/inference-usw-2). ETA ~3m.
Dawn: restarting kubelet on node_gpu_03 (systemctl restart kubelet)
Dawn: kubelet restarted, journald shows kubelet started at 10:18:42 UTC. Node transitioned to Ready at 10:19:05.
Priya: node_gpu_03 now Ready. node_gpu_07 still NotReady. For node_gpu_07 I see repeated nvidia driver timeouts (NVRM) and a lot of oom_kill logs.
Matt R: I've adjusted smart routing: shifted ~40% of inference traffic away from inference-pool-usw-2 to inference-pool-usw-1 as fallback, reduced new session creation to this pool. Traffic drop effective now. p50/p95 improving halfway.
Matt R: metrics snapshot after initial mitigations:
```
p50: 210ms -> was 1200ms
p95: 680ms -> was 3800ms
5xx rate: 1.3% -> was 12%
```
Shilpa: Good. Priya, can you force-recreate any evicted GPU pods onto new nodes? Also ensure the rogue training job is cordoned and ticketed.
Priya: Force-deleting remaining GPU-local pods and re-creating on new nodes. Using nodeSelector to avoid placing training jobs into inference pool: adding label `role=inference` to autoscaler config.
Priya: drain on node_gpu_07 still stuck due to device-plugin crash; plan to reboot the node if driver restarts don't stabilize. Are we comfortable rebooting?
Dawn: I'll attempt driver reload first: `modprobe -r nvidia` then `modprobe nvidia`, if that fails, do a reboot.
Dawn: modprobe failed (kernel refused full unload), scheduling node reboot now. Reboot initiated at 10:28:12 UTC.
Infra Bot: new instances are up and joining the cluster (node_gpu_15, node_gpu_16).
Dawn: node_gpu_07 came back after reboot, but kubelet started slowly; there are CUDA initialization warnings but node becomes Ready at 10:33:40. Will keep monitoring GPU Xids.
Matt R: Post-recovery metrics look stable, 5xx back to baseline ~0.5%, p95 ~250ms. No customer-facing alerts open.
Shilpa: Handing off monitoring to next oncall (Dawn) in ~20m. Follow-ups created:
- TICKET-4021: Investigate GPU driver Xid 79 frequency across fleet, kernel/driver compatibility matrix (Priya)
- TICKET-4022: Block non-inference training jobs from inference pool via admission webhook (Matt R)
- TICKET-4023: Add node auto-replace on repeated kubelet restarts (Infra)
Priya: Created TICKET-4021 and linked logs /nvidia/xid/ with sample core dumps.
Shilpa: Any customer impact to escalate to SRE/Product? Looks like degraded latency for ~12 minutes for a subset of tenants — I'll draft a short status note.
Matt R: No high-severity customer incidents reported; recommend monitoring window 2h and keep routing fallback ready.
incident-bot: Incident state -> MONITORING. Happy to re-open if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
Shilpa: Thanks everyone — will follow up on the action items during next-day postmortem.
Dawn: leaving notes in runbook and linking node/kernel logs. :spiral_note_pad:
